why: A new original game on the engine (the user's Burn Rate request, 2026-10-23) must not show LF2 2.0a's own strings: its title screen drew "by Marti Wong, Starsky Wong / 1999-2008, all rights reserved / http://www.LittleFighter.com" and its window was titled "Little Fighter 2".
decision: The EXE strings a player sees become game values carried by OriginalGameRules.Branding, LF2 2.0a's by default; this reverses E3b's "the EXE's own strings stay" for these strings only (the DAT key and the cheat sequences stay).

randori.commit: 786befd (Let a game supply the branding strings)

design.fields: windowClass, windowTitle, shortName (quit caption and "LF2" in two replay errors), credits (three plain lines of exactly 27, 30 and 28 printable ASCII bytes; encoded for the EXE model's copy as plain[i] &+ (i & 3) plus NUL), creditLinks (3), website, controlHelp, recordingHelp, challenge, advertise, forum, builtInBackgroundName (<= 29)
design.validation: a throwing public init (Branding.Invalid(field:)); .lf2 through an internal non-throwing init, checked by a test running the public checks; windowClass/windowTitle/shortName printable ASCII
design.defaults: OriginalGameRules.lf2(...) defaults to Branding.lf2; the full OriginalGameRules.init requires a branding; public entry points take a defaulted parameter; OriginalApplicationMenuSession.State holds the game's branding (no default) and the loaded menu takes it from there
